title: Prolyl-isomerase Pin1 drives platinum resistance by regulating Notch3 stability and function in ovarian cancer.
authors: Giuli, Maria Valeria; Mancusi, Angelica; Natiello, Bianca; Di Cristofano, Samuele; Reali, Rebecca; Pignataro, Maria Gemma; D'Andrea, Daniel; Di Magno, Laura; Nicoletti, Carmine; Giorgi, Alessandra; Macone, Alberto; Camerini, Serena; Casella, Marialuisa; Peruzzi, Giovanna; Zema, Sabrina; Canettieri, Gianluca; Tomao, Federica; Palaia, Innocenza; Pernazza, Angelina; Rustighi, Alessandra; Palermo, Rocco; Raimondo, Domenico; Monti, Alessandra; Doti, Nunzianna; d'Amati, Giulia; Del Sal, Giannino; Screpanti, Isabella; Talora, Claudio; Bellavia, Diana; Checquolo, Saula
journal: Journal of experimental & clinical cancer research : CR
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Pin1与Notch3蛋白互作驱动卵巢癌铂耐药，虽含分子对接与动力学模拟，但核心是蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Resistance to platinum-based drugs represents a major obstacle for the management of high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) patients. Indeed, the selective pressure of platinum-based (PT) chemotherapy often leads to the outgrowth of platinum-resistant subclones. In this scenario, the underlying adaptive networks should be fully investigated to provide advances toward more streamlined and personalized care. METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive analysis of Pin1/Notch3relationship from HGSOC cell lines and primary tumours, integrating multiple genetic targeting under chemotherapy pressure, differential proteomic approaches, molecular docking data and dynamics simulations, thus identifying a functional circuit evaluated in vitro and in vivo models.We conducted a comprehensive analysis of relationship from HGSOC cell lines and primary tumours, integrating multiple genetic targeting under chemotherapy pressure, differential proteomic approaches, molecular docking data and dynamics simulations, thus identifying a functional circuit evaluated in vitro and in vivo models. RESULTS: Here, we demonstrated that carboplatin treatment of HGSOC cells promoted the activation of the Pin1/Notch3 axis, resulting in platinum resistance. Accordingly, HGSOC-bearing patients showing increased Pin1/Notch3 co-expression after PT-based chemotherapy correlated with a clinical worse response. Conversely, genetic targeting of Pin1 combined with carboplatin treatment sensitizes resistant cells to platinum-based therapy, both in vitro and in vivo, strongly reducing their Notch3-mediated metastatic potential in preclinical murine models. Mechanistically, Pin1-Notch3 binding favours protection of Notch3 from its GSK3beta-mediated degradation, resulting in increased Notch3 expression. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, our findings identify the functional Pin1/Notch3 axis as an escape strategy from chemotherapy-induced cell death, thus suggesting a novel predictive role of the Pin1/Notch3 axis in the platinum response, which could be useful for implementing frontline treatments for HGSOC patients before recurrence.
abstract_zh: 背景：对铂类药物耐药是高级别浆液性卵巢癌（HGSOC）患者管理中的主要障碍。事实上，铂类（PT）化疗的选择性压力常导致铂耐药亚克隆的生长。在此情况下，应充分研究潜在的适应性网络，以推动更简化和个性化护理的进展。方法：我们对HGSOC细胞系和原发肿瘤中Pin1/Notch3关系进行了全面分析，整合了化疗压力下的多重遗传靶向、差异蛋白质组学方法、分子对接数据和动力学模拟，从而识别出一个在体外和体内模型中评估的功能回路。我们对HGSOC细胞系和原发肿瘤中关系进行了全面分析，整合了化疗压力下的多重遗传靶向、差异蛋白质组学方法、分子对接数据和动力学模拟，从而识别出一个在体外和体内模型中评估的功能回路。结果：在此，我们证明卡铂处理HGSOC细胞促进了Pin1/Notch3轴的激活，导致铂耐药。相应地，PT化疗后显示Pin1/Notch3共表达增加的HGSOC患者与临床较差反应相关。相反，Pin1的遗传靶向结合卡铂处理，在体外和体内均使耐药细胞对铂类治疗敏感，并在临床前小鼠模型中显著降低其Notch3介导的转移潜力。机制上，Pin1-Notch3结合有利于保护Notch3免受其GSK3β介导的降解，导致Notch3表达增加。结论：总体而言，我们的发现将功能性Pin1/Notch3轴识别为化疗诱导细胞死亡的逃逸策略，从而提示Pin1/Notch3轴在铂反应中的新型预测作用，这可能有助于在复发前为HGSOC患者实施一线治疗。
